a1_answer:
NOVELTY STATEMENT — Standard practice tracks overall vibration energy (RMS or peak) which only rises significantly when spalling is advanced. My observable is the rate of change of the vibration envelope's kurtosis, which increases as early-stage spalling creates impulsive forces that initially appear as outliers in the vibration signal before they contribute significantly to overall energy. This captures the early-stage defect signature that RMS methods miss.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is that early spalling creates high-frequency impulses with low energy but high amplitude, increasing the kurtosis (fourth moment) of the vibration signal. For a healthy bearing, kurtosis ≈ 3 (Gaussian distribution). With early spalling, kurtosis can increase to 5-10 while RMS remains near baseline. A rate of change of 0.1/day over 3 consecutive days provides sufficient sensitivity to detect this change before RMS-based alarms would trigger.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — Components: 1) Existing 1 kHz vibration accelerometer, 2) Existing SCADA system, 3) Standard signal processing software (e.g., MATLAB, Python with NumPy). Procedure: 1) Log 1-second vibration samples every 10 minutes (6 samples/hour), 2) Compute envelope of each sample using Hilbert transform, 3) Calculate kurtosis of envelope for each sample, 4) Compute daily rate of change of kurtosis (slope of linear fit over 24 hourly averages), 5) Flag when rate of change exceeds threshold for 3 consecutive days. All processing uses standard libraries and runs on existing infrastructure.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Installability: Same (no new hardware). Operability: Same (uses existing SCADA interface). Maintenance: Same (no additional maintenance requirements). Cost class: Same (software-only solution). The only difference is the algorithm processing the same data stream, making the deployment burden identical to standard vibration monitoring while providing earlier detection.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: 1) Install test system on 10 identical fan drives with 5 healthy bearings and 5 with artificially induced early spalling, 2) Monitor for 90 days, 3) Record all alarms and bearing conditions. Pass/Fail Threshold: System must detect all 5 spalled bearings at least 14 days before failure while producing no more than 2 false alarms across all 10 fans. Duration: 90 days. Kill Criterion: If more than 2 false alarms occur OR if any spalled bearing is detected less than 14 days before failure, the predictor is falsified and must be redesigned.
